column3: “Answered and said” is rendered “answered.”
The Hebrew reads “my destruction” (written “my calamity”); NASB has “my iniquity.” “People will raise” is rendered “laid.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“With me” is rendered “within me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The slime of purslane” is rendered “the white of an egg”; the meaning of the Hebrew words is uncertain.
“Like the illness of my food” is rendered “like loathsome food”; the Hebrew is difficult.
“Who will give” is rendered “Oh that”; “hope” is rendered “longing.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“May I jump in anguish which does not relent” is rendered “I rejoice in unsparing pain”; the meaning of the verb is uncertain. “Hidden” is rendered “denied.”
“That I will prolong my life” is rendered “that I should endure.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Sound wisdom” is rendered “deliverance.”
The Hebrew is difficult; NASB supplies “there should be” and “So that he does not.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Hides itself” is rendered “melts.”
“When they flow” is rendered “When they become waterless”; the meaning of the verb is uncertain.
“They twist the paths” is rendered “The paths … wind along.” It may mean caravans turn aside; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“He had been confident” is rendered “they had trusted.”
The written Hebrew reads “not” and the reading aloud “to it”; NASB follows the latter. NASB supplies “such.”
NASB supplies “something” and “Or.”
NASB supplies “Or.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“How painful are words of uprightness” follows one reading of the verb; it may mean “forceful.” “From you” is rendered “your argument.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“You will make fall” is rendered “cast lots”; NASB supplies “lots.”
“Be willing, turn on me” is rendered “please look at me”; NASB supplies “see.”
“Turn back” is rendered “Desist.” NASB follows the reading aloud in the second line.
Close to the Hebrew.
